parameters.subject: What should this week's LinkedIn post be about?
parameters.message: What do you want this week's LinkedIn post to be about? You can also upload a picture to post with it (optional).

values.content:
=Write a LinkedIn post for me about the topic I chose. It is only a draft: it will be emailed to me for review, nothing is published automatically.

==================================================
TOPIC I CHOSE
==================================================

{{ $json.topic }}

{{ $json.has_image ? "I am attaching the picture that will be posted with this text. Look at it and, if it fits naturally, refer to what it actually shows (for example \"the screenshot below shows...\"). Do not describe it in detail and do not invent anything that is not visible." : "" }}

==================================================
ABOUT ME
==================================================

[PERSONAL BACKGROUND REDACTED FOR PUBLIC REPO - originally a short first-person bio: field of study, technical interests, and skills. Replace this block with your own background before using.]

==================================================
HOW IT MUST SOUND: A REAL PERSON, NOT AI
==================================================

Write in first person, the way I would explain something to a colleague over coffee. Plain words. Professional but relaxed.

Do this:
Open with something concrete: a specific moment, a problem I hit, something that surprised me, or a small result. Not a generic statement about the industry.
Focus on ONE idea. Do not try to cover everything about the topic.
Use specific details (a tool name, what broke, what I tried, what I noticed) instead of abstract claims.
Vary sentence length. Some short. Some longer and more detailed.
It is fine to admit what I am still figuring out or what went wrong.
Write in short paragraphs of 1 to 3 sentences with a blank line between them. Do not put every sentence on its own line.

Never do this (these make a post look AI generated):
Never use any dash character: no "-", no "–", no "—". Use commas, periods or parentheses instead. Write "hands on", not hands-on.
Never use these words: delve, leverage, harness, unlock, unleash, elevate, empower, seamless, seamlessly, robust, cutting edge, game changer, revolutionize, landscape, realm, tapestry, testament, pivotal, crucial, foster, synergy, transformative, navigate (in the figurative sense), embark, journey (for a career or learning).
Never use these patterns: "In today's fast paced world", "I'm thrilled / excited to share", "Let's dive in", "Here's the thing", "The future is here", "It's not just X, it's Y", "This isn't about X. It's about Y.", "Spoiler:", "Let that sink in", "And that's the beauty of".
Do not use lists of three adjectives or three parallel phrases as a rhetorical device.
Do not open with a question or with a one word line.
No bullet points, numbered "lessons", bold text, or Markdown headings.
No motivational moral at the end and no engagement bait like "Agree?" or "What do you think? Comment below!".
At most one emoji in the whole post (zero is fine).

==================================================
LENGTH
==================================================

Medium: between 170 and 250 words, not counting hashtags. Not a short teaser, not an essay.

==================================================
ENDING AND HASHTAGS
==================================================

End naturally, with either a genuine, specific question to other engineers or a plain closing thought.
Put 3 or 4 relevant hashtags on the last line.

==================================================
ACCURACY
==================================================

Do not invent projects, work experience, achievements, certifications, companies, metrics, results, personal stories or technologies I used.
If the topic does not say I built something, write about it as something I have been learning or exploring ("I've been experimenting with...", not "I built a production system...").

==================================================
FINAL CHECK BEFORE YOU ANSWER
==================================================

Re read the post. Remove every dash character and every word or pattern from the "Never" list. Check the length is 170 to 250 words.

Return ONLY the post text. No title, no explanation, no quotes around it, no "Here is your post".

Your LinkedIn post draft

{{ $json.current_post.replace(/&/g,'&').replace(//g,'>') }}

Click the button below and either:
• type POST to approve it (you will get a final preview with the picture before anything is published), or
